messages:
elaine_sales: NovaHealth POC: intermittent timeouts on mixed TS frontend + Python backend behind corporate proxy. ~5-10% fail with \"upstream timeout\" and occasional 502s. Exec demo next week, need quick triage. Anyone available?
ben_engineering: I can jump in. can you share logs and which SDK versions? my hunch: connection reuse / keepalive mismatch across SDKs with proxy.
elaine_sales: logs from their dev cluster:
```
2025-06-02T09:12:03Z ERROR request_id=abcd1234 upstream_error=\"504 Gateway Timeout\" route=/v1/generate client=python-sdk
2025-06-02T09:12:03Z WARN request_id=abcd1234 retry_attempt=1 reason=stream-reset
2025-06-02T09:12:04Z INFO request_id=efgh5678 ts-client idle_reuse=true
```
They say TS client succeeds more often; concurrent traffic makes python time out. Using python sdk v0.9.3 (requests) and ts sdk v1.1.2. Proxy: https://proxy.sawtooth.local:8443, auth token, HTTPS_PROXY set, NO_PROXY not set.
priya_support: common issue. python requests + corporate forward proxies often open new TCPs instead of reusing, hitting proxy limits. Are they using Session pooling?
ravi_sre: also check proxy per-IP concurrent connection caps and session affinity. Some proxies do cookie-based balancing that interacts badly with keepalive.
ben_engineering: quick mitigations: 1) add NO_PROXY for our endpoints so traffic bypasses corporate proxy; 2) enable a persistent HTTPAdapter in python with larger pool; 3) tune retries/backoff. If NO_PROXY not possible, force aggressive pooling and HTTP/1.1 keepalive.
priya_support: sample python patch we recommend:
```
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
import requests
s = requests.Session()
retries = Retry(total=5, backoff_factor=0.4, status_forcelist=[429,502,503,504])
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_maxsize=100, max_retries=retries, pool_block=True))
# pass this session into the Redwood client transport
```
ben_engineering: node snippet for keepalive:
```
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 50 });
const client = new RedwoodClient({ transport: { agent } });
```
priya_support: also ensure retries use jitter and respect 429 to avoid thundering herd against proxy.
elaine_sales: customer asked if Dedicated helps here and cost implications.
ben_engineering: Dedicated reduces noisy-neighbor issues on our side but does not bypass their corporate proxy. Private (VPC/on-prem) eliminates proxy path. For pricing we need their expected QPS and token throughput; I can draft a sizing + cost note.
ravi_sre: troubleshooting checklist: capture client-side connection stats (socket counts, TIME_WAIT), proxy logs for per-IP connection limits, and test with NO_PROXY toggled. If they can't set NO_PROXY, try pooling + shorter client chunk timeouts.
secops_bot: on privacy: we log source IP at edge for metrics; headers are not stored by default except routing headers. For PII-sensitive workloads recommend Private deployment + KMS and controlled audit logs. I'll share a short FAQ.
priya_support: action items: ben -> push python sample + repro script that toggles NO_PROXY and prints connection stats; ravi -> run proxy cap checklist; secops_bot -> send FAQ and redacted logging policy; elaine -> ask customer to run repro and share results by EOD.
deploybot: deploy note: these are client-side fixes, no infra changes required.
ben_engineering: one more tip: if they see stream resets, reduce client chunk timeout and enable reconnect that can resume from KV cache if supported (saves tokens). I'll include pointers in the patch.
elaine_sales: thanks, I'll coordinate the test and update the exec prep. tagging @novah-cto to request NO_PROXY check and proxy logs :thumbsup:
priya_support: standing by to jump on a call with the customer if needed :phone:
secops_bot: posted FAQ link (private) with recommended config and redaction notes.
elaine_sales: will close loop here after tests. thanks team!
